title.narrative: Sustaining Continuum Primary Healthcare Service Delivery to vulnerable affected populations in Damboa

description.narrative:
ltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif font-size: 8pt"gtIn line with the Nigeria Humanitarian Response Plan 2023, Action Health Incorporated (AHI) seeks to strengthen access to Vulnerable and Affected populations (Girls, women, boys, men) from different communities (IDPs, returnees, people in extremely-hard–to-reach areas and host populations) in Damboa LGA, Borno State to basic quality life-saving primary health service. These services will be guided by the following principles: community participation, equity, equality, safety, and accountability.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gt
lt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtThe affected population will receive a comprehensive Essential Health Service Package, IMCI for children under 5 years, MISP, and MHPSS, especially for adolescent girls and women. There will be an increasing focus on outreach services through Mobile Health Teams, including health promotion activities and referrals with special attention for vulnerable persons including people with disabilities (PwD)ltbrgtltbrgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtProposed activities arelt/spangtlta style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gt. Training for healthcare workers (8 Nurses and 12 CHEWs)lt/agtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtnbspon nbspICCM/ IPC and deployment of these health workers asnbspMobile Medical Teams to extremely hard-to-reach communities Provision of continuous primary health services in communities with high gaps including services on Integrated Management of Childhood iIllness(IMCI) and complicated SAM cases Provision of reproductive health services including nbspANC and Post Natal care, Childbirth care (using delivery kits for clean/safe deliveries)nbspand Family Planning services andnbspadequate referrals for complicated cases in extremely hard to reach communities Cholera, malaria, and typhoid active case search and case management with bolstering Risk Communication and Community Engagement. Procurement and Pre-positioning of Essential medicines and supplies, malaria and cholera kits and support referrals to secondary health care services.nbspltbrgtltbrgtlt/spangtltspan style="color: black"gtltfont face="Arial, sans-serif"gtAdopting the humanitarian-development nexus approach, this project will reinforce the quality continuum of care in the existing 4 PHCs (General Hospital IDP camp, Family Support Clinic, Nzuba PHC, and Shuwari PHC) and set up lt/fontgtltagtltfont face="Arial, sans-serif"gt4 Mobile Medical Teams comprising of (2 nurses and 3 CHEWs)nbsp per teamnbsplt/fontgtlt/agtlt/spangtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtto reach women, men, children, elderly, and persons with disabilities (PWDslt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="color: black font-family: Arial, sans-serif font-size: 8pt"gtThe project will significantly improve access to quality comprehensive and inclusive healthcare services and increase the well-being of the vulnerable affected population in Damboa LGA, Borno Statelt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgt
